title: Wang variant rotation per bitmask — N/E/S/W edge cells use SAME mesh with proper Y rotation (fix '4-variant-collapse' feel)
intent: S170 (Wang integration) + S176 (grass family) ship with a 16→4 lookup table that maps ALL edge bitmasks (1, 2, 4, 8) to variant 0 — meaning N-edge, S-edge, E-edge, W-edge cells all use the SAME mesh, undifferentiated. Same for corners + T-junctions — all collapse to variant 1. Result: 'набор кубов' visual feel — adjacent edge cells don't visibly stitch, they tile like a textbook autotile bug. The fix is small: each variant index has a CANONICAL ORIENTATION (variant 0 = N-edge canonical), and the bitmask→variant lookup ALSO returns a Y-rotation that orients the canonical mesh to match the actual bitmask. 16 bitmasks → 4 mesh shapes × 4 rotations = 16 visually distinct cells from 4 procedural builders. Zero new mesh code. ~30 LOC change to the lookup table + rotation application at mesh-spawn time.
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-29 — current Wang tiles look like 'набор кубов'. Audit of `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/wang-family-lookup.ts` confirms 16→4 collapse without rotation. This is the smallest-cost, highest-impact correction in the visual track. After this lands, the same 4 procedural builders from S165 give 16 visually distinct outcomes — adjacent edge cells naturally point outward in the right direction. Marked `should` because the existing tile look is functionally OK; this is correctness-of-readability work.
acceptanceHints: TARGET FILE: `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/wang-family-lookup.ts`. Existing lookup table is `LOOKUP_TABLE: number[16]` returning variant indices only — extend to return { variantIndex: number, rotationYDeg: number } tuples.
TARGET DOWNSTREAM: per-cell mesh spawn site (wherever the spawner reads currentVariantIndex from WangTile component) — apply the rotation when creating the mesh entity's Transform.
CANONICAL ORIENTATION CONVENTION:

Variant 0 (edge) — canonical orientation = N-edge (open face facing NORTH). Bitmask 8 (N neighbour, i.e. NORTH cell IS same-family) means the SOUTH side of THIS cell is the open boundary — rotate variant 0 by 180° so the open face points SOUTH.
Variant 1 (corner / T) — canonical = NW corner (open W + open N).
Variant 2 (filler) — surrounded, no rotation needed (symmetric).
Variant 3 (isolated) — no neighbours, no rotation needed (radially symmetric).
REVISED LOOKUP TABLE (16 entries, each = { variantIndex, rotationYDeg }):
// Bitmask N=8, E=4, S=2, W=1
// bit set = neighbour IS same-family
// The 'open face' rotation orients the mesh so its edge detail faces AWAY from same-family neighbours.
bitmask  0 (0000, isolated)             → { variantIndex: 3, rotationYDeg: 0 }
bitmask  1 (0001, W neighbour)          → { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 90 }
bitmask  2 (0010, S neighbour)          → { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 180 }
bitmask  3 (0011, S+W neighbours)       → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 180 } (NE corner — open N + E)
bitmask  4 (0100, E neighbour)          → { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 270 }
bitmask  5 (0101, E+W)                  → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 0 } REUSED — actually a 'straight wall N-S' — distinct from corner. NEEDS variant 4 or a special straight case. SEE BELOW.
bitmask  6 (0110, E+S)                  → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 270 } (NW corner — open N + W)
bitmask  7 (0111, E+S+W)                → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 270 } (open N only, T-junction)
bitmask  8 (1000, N neighbour)          → { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 0 } (canonical)
bitmask  9 (1001, N+W)                  → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 90 } (SE corner)
bitmask 10 (1010, N+S)                  → straight wall E-W — same as bitmask 5 issue
bitmask 11 (1011, N+S+W)                → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 90 } (open E only)
bitmask 12 (1100, N+E)                  → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 0 } (SW corner)
bitmask 13 (1101, N+E+W)                → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 0 } (open S only)
bitmask 14 (1110, N+E+S)                → { variantIndex: 1, rotationYDeg: 180 } (open W only)
bitmask 15 (1111, surrounded)           → { variantIndex: 2, rotationYDeg: 0 } (filler)
STRAIGHT-WALL CASE (bitmasks 5 + 10):
Bitmask 5 (E+W) = a horizontal corridor cell (wall extends E-W; N+S open). Bitmask 10 (N+S) = vertical corridor.
These don't fit variant 0 (single-edge) NOR variant 1 (corner with two open sides AT angles). They need a new variant 4 = 'straight wall' (both open sides parallel, mesh symmetric on the wall axis).
OPTION A — Add a 5th procedural builder: 'straight wall' with edge detail on both open faces.
OPTION B — Reuse variant 1 (corner) but acknowledge visual oddness (corner-style detail on a straight wall reads as 'bent' wall).
RECOMMENDATION A: add the 5th builder. ~50 LOC for each family. The straight-wall case is common in arena layouts (long corridors).
BUILDER UPDATES — add 5th variant per family:
hard-block-variants.ts: add buildHardBlockVariant4 = 'straight-wall' (panel-block flanked by smooth sides on the open-faces).
soft-block-variants.ts: add buildSoftBlockVariant4 = 'plank wall' (planks extending parallel to the wall axis).
floor-tile-variants.ts (if shipped): add buildFloorTileVariant4 = 'narrow path' (lane-shaped).
grass family (from S176): add buildGrassVariant4 = 'long grass strip'.
ROTATION APPLICATION AT MESH SPAWN:
Wang resolver writes currentVariantIndex + currentMeshKey on WangTile component. NEW: writes currentRotationYDeg too (or use the existing variant.rotationY field per wang-tile-variant.schema.json).
Mesh spawn system (per project) reads currentRotationYDeg + applies to spawned mesh entity's Transform.rotation.y.
Implementation: extend bitmaskToVariant() to return the tuple. Update WangTile component schema to carry currentRotationYDeg. Update the per-cell mesh spawner to apply rotation.
FAMILY-AGNOSTIC FIX:

The lookup table change applies to hard-block + soft-block + grass + (future) path/stone/dirt/floor families. Single 16-entry lookup table generates 16 distinct visual outcomes from 4-5 procedural builders × 4 rotations.
ENGINE WANG MODULE EXTENSION:
Engine WangTileVariant schema already has `rotationY?` field per wang-tile-variant.schema.json (per GDP-002 spec). This story uses it.
Engine resolver: variant lookup returns rotationY from the family's variants[bitmask].rotationY field. Project's lookup table populates the variants[].rotationY per the table above.
TESTS:
bitmaskToVariant(1) returns { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 90 }.
bitmaskToVariant(8) returns { variantIndex: 0, rotationYDeg: 0 }.
bitmaskToVariant(5) returns { variantIndex: 4, rotationYDeg: 0 } (after adding 5th builder).
Mesh spawn: cell at bitmask 4 gets rotation 270° applied to Transform.rotation.y.
Visual snapshot test: 5-cell horizontal wall (bitmasks 1, 5, 5, 5, 4 from W to E) renders as a connected wall with end-pieces facing outward, NOT as 5 identical wooden crates.
VISUAL QA:
Load default arena → soft blocks rendered as a wall now visibly connect (edges face outward, corners face inward).
Walk around the arena — corners feel like corners, edges like edges, fillers like fillers.
No two cells visually identical when their bitmasks differ.
4-cell row of soft blocks reads as a wall, not 4 separate crates.
PERFORMANCE: zero. Rotation is a Transform field; engine handles it.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Mirror flag (mirrorX, mirrorZ) variants. Some corner positions could benefit from mirror in addition to rotation; v1 uses rotation only.
More than 5 variant builders per family. 5 is the design budget for v1.
Sub-variant random pick (cell A and cell B with same bitmask use the same mesh + same rotation). Sub-variants are a separate story (visual-style-md §3.5).
Per-theme rotation overrides (themes don't affect rotation, only palette).
